source.meaning: The actual clause requires identifying Canada’s provinces and territories and their capitals, and describing location and some peoples living there. The proposed card accounts only for the location/name/capital knowledge; the attributed peoples/resource task remains separately required.

reuseComparison.name: Australia’s states and territories
reuseComparison.mismatch: Requires Australia’s actual six states/ACT/NT/capitals and recognition of its other territories. These explicit different answers remain intact. Mastering them does not establish Canada’s13pairs; replacing Australia with Canada would overwrite a real factual claim, not merely localize an example.

reuseComparison.name: Local, regional and state scales
reuseComparison.mismatch: Representing own place at several scales and a cross-scale interconnection does not establish the complete Canadian province/territory-capital knowledge set.

reuseComparison.name: Reading and drawing maps
reuseComparison.mismatch: A labelled map can be read correctly without knowing the identities/locations/capital pairs when the answer labels change or are absent. Generic key/relative-location/construction operation is preserved as shared support.

reuseComparison.name: Grid references and directions
reuseComparison.mismatch: Locating a named cell/path does not establish which province or capital the location is.

reuseComparison.name: Ontario communities and local governance
reuseComparison.mismatch: Municipal/FN/Métis institutional roles and service/development authority differ from the national province/territory/capital map inventory. No Canadian constitutional powers are added to that old card.

reuseComparison.name: Traditional and treaty territories in Canada
reuseComparison.mismatch: Locally verified territory/treaty/reserve distinctions are not this province/capital knowledge, and provincial boundaries do not establish Indigenous territories.

reuseComparison.name: Ontario’s major landform regions
reuseComparison.mismatch: Physical regional knowledge is not a political subdivision or capital inventory.

independentAssessment.positive: Names/locates13 divisions and associates capitals after learning, distinguishes Ottawa/Toronto roles and transfers across a changed political map.
nearMiss: Copies a fully labelled map but cannot identify the same places without labels.
Uses the largest familiar city as capital, e.g.Vancouver rather than Victoria.
Calls Ottawa the capital of Ontario or treats Ontario as a physical landform region.
independentAssessment.transfer: Use a differently coloured/styled, clearly legible Canada reference with equivalent broad locations and ask for region/capital associations and one relative location; do not test obscure map projections or tiny exact dots.
independentAssessment.contrast: A learner can know all Australian pairs or correctly use a new grid/key but know none of these Canadian pairs. Conversely Canadian name/location knowledge does not establish map construction or legal jurisdictional relationships.

whyNotAnotherProcedureOrGradeClone: The independently missing answers are a bounded national factual representation, not a different grade of generic map skill or one node per province. Old Australian and generic claims remain fully preserved. No country change is inferred to transfer learner mastery.

proposedContribution.remainingSourceCondition: The actual some-peoples-in-the-regions requirement needs an attributed location/people resource/task design, not a stereotype or population fact inferred from this map. B3.4institutional powers and B3overall also remain separate.

consumerImpact: New claim only if independent boundary approved. Preserve all old IDs/cards/guides/contexts and no inferred learner-state transfer. Same Canada knowledge could be reused by later source slices instead of new grade-specific copies.

newCard.subject: Geography
newCard.name: Canada’s provinces, territories and capitals
newCard.description: Know Canada’s ten provinces and three territories, locate them broadly on a political map and pair each with its provincial or territorial capital. Distinguish these capitals from Canada’s national capital, Ottawa, and recognize the same places in a changed map style rather than rely on one colour scheme.
evidence: Name and broadly locate the ten provinces and three territories, distinguishing the two groups, without copying a complete visible answer list.
Associate each province/territory with its capital and broadly locate those capitals; distinguish a provincial/territorial capital from Ottawa’s national-capital role.

Recognize the same political geography in a differently styled map and explain supported broad relative locations; no current population, language proficiency, legal boundary or detailed government-powers claim.
newCard.assessmentPrompt: After studying a Canada map, can {{name}} name and broadly locate its ten provinces and three territories and pair each with its capital, without the answer labels? Why are Ottawa and Toronto different kinds of capital? Try a differently styled map too. Correct oral English or French names and broad pointing count; this is not a spelling or surveying test.

pedagogy.summary: Study the verified political map and capital pairs, retrieve the names/locations, then transfer to a differently styled map. Original untested design; no instructional-effectiveness claim.
bestPractices: Keep province/territory names, capital names and capital roles distinct.
Use legible large views or insets for small Atlantic provinces and nearby capital labels, alongside the national overview.
Retrieve the complete 13 division/capital set after study; do not mistake copying labels for retained knowledge.
Accept accurate oral English or French place names; no accent, spelling or exact-border-tracing demand.
keyRepresentations: Actual Canada political map with legible capital-symbol key
A differently styled map or unlabelled outline retaining reliable geographic reference
commonMisconceptions: The largest or most famous city must be the capital.
A political map establishes Indigenous traditional or treaty territories.
A different map colour changes the place or its status.

learn.summary: Connect Canada’s complete 13 division/capital set with broad locations, retrieve it and transfer across legible maps.

activities.title: Study names, places and capital roles
learnerActions: Use the verified table with the actual political map. Name all ten provinces and three territories, locating their broad positions and matching each with its capital. Keep both groups explicit; repeated short study sessions can build the complete set without changing the eventual claim.

Read the map’s capital key. Compare Toronto, Ontario’s provincial capital, with Ottawa, Canada’s national capital located in Ontario. Compare Victoria with Vancouver and Québec/Quebec City with Montréal as checks against assuming largest/famous city means capital.
Provide an enlarged Atlantic view or labelled inset where needed, maintaining its relation to the national view. Use broad pointing or a marker, not precise surveyed city coordinates.
Compare verified broad relative positions using the actual map reference. Treat small-island/nearby-label legibility as a resource issue, not a harder spelling or fine-motor test.
activities.intendedInsight: Political divisions, their capitals and the national-capital role are distinct named geographical knowledge.
feedback: Return to the actual capital symbol and verified pair when a famous-city answer replaces the capital.
Show an enlarged source view when a small province or label cannot be read.
activities.rationale: Original source-fit design; not a tested memorization intervention.
sourceClaims: The current federal provinces-and-territories table identifies ten provinces and three territories and lists the13 provincial/territorial capital pairs.

The actual NRCan Canada reference map labels those political divisions and capitals, distinguishing the national capital in its key; this dated map is used only for the verified stable political geography.

activities.title: Retrieve and transfer the complete knowledge set
learnerActions: After study, remove answer labels and the completed pair table. Ask the learner to name/broadly locate all 13 divisions, distinguish the ten provinces from the three territories, and name their capitals. Prompt in a changed order; a list copied from a visible key is not this check.

Have the learner mark or point to broad capital locations and explain the Ottawa/Toronto distinction. Accept correct English or French names, including Québec for Quebec City in clear city context and Terre-Neuve-et-Labrador for Newfoundland and Labrador. Do not introduce spelling marks.

Repeat selected locations/capital matches on a differently styled accurate map or outline. Ensure the national overview, insets and reference are legible rather than testing tiny-print recognition or memorized colours.

Ask what the political map does NOT show: these boundaries/capital symbols alone do not establish Indigenous traditional/treaty territories, all local peoples, population facts or the detailed powers of governments. Those are separate source/task questions.
activities.intendedInsight: Recall and cross-map recognition establish this factual representation rather than copying one coloured map.
feedback: Re-study a mistaken pair, then check it in a changed order/view; retain a partial result if any required division/capital remains unsupported.
Separate a capital-role mistake from a map-reading or name-legibility problem.
activities.rationale: Original untested diagnostic and transfer design.
sourceClaims: The current federal provinces-and-territories table identifies ten provinces and three territories and lists the13 provincial/territorial capital pairs.

The actual NRCan Canada reference map labels those political divisions and capitals, distinguishing the national capital in its key; this dated map is used only for the verified stable political geography.

constraints: This is one bounded knowledge set, not 13 topics or age/difficulty tiers.
No mandatory exact spelling, precise city coordinate, surveying, population inventory, detailed government powers or exhaustive peoples inventory.
Political boundaries are not Indigenous traditional/treaty territory boundaries.

Use the current verified capital table with the dated 2006 map only for corroborated stable names/locations. Exclude outdated magnetic-pole/ice data and unrelated unverified population/devolution prose.
Source B3.5 peoples/location descriptions require a separate attributed case protocol; this new card alone does not certify that entire expectation.
No hard prerequisites inferred merely from source order; map-operation support can be supplied without changing existing claims.
reviewNotes: 2026-11-10: original teaching design following cross-domain whole-claim search and independent grain/source challenge. Factual sources verified; teaching efficacy untested.

assess.diagnosticPrompt: After studying a Canada map, can {{name}} name and broadly locate its ten provinces and three territories and pair each with its capital, without the answer labels? Why are Ottawa and Toronto different kinds of capital? Try a differently styled map too. Correct oral English or French names and broad pointing count; this is not a spelling or surveying test.
assess.correctAnswer: Names and broadly locates the complete ten-province/three-territory set; pairs each with its correct capital and broadly locates it; distinguishes Ottawa’s national role from provincial/territorial capitals and transfers to a changed accurate map. Correct oral English/French names count.
assess.whatMakesItDiscriminate: Removing labels separates retrieved factual knowledge from copying; famous-city and Ottawa/Toronto contrasts distinguish capital roles; a changed map style and legible insets test geographic recognition rather than colour or tiny-print memorization.
probeDeeper: Which place is the capital, and which map symbol or studied fact supports it?
Does a larger city necessarily have the capital role?
Can you find the same place on this different map? What does the political map not establish?

errorPatterns.pattern: Substitutes a famous/larger city or confuses national and provincial capital roles.
errorPatterns.revealedBy: Vancouver for Victoria, Montréal for Québec/Quebec City, or Ottawa for Ontario’s capital.
errorPatterns.nextMove: Compare the verified pair table and actual key; retrieve the pair/role again without visible answers on a changed map.

responseLevels.full: Complete13 division/capital set with broad locations, correct capital-role distinctions and changed-map recognition; no spelling or survey precision requirement.
